title: Settlement Agreements Between a Plan and a Party in Interest
source_verification_depth: Complete Supporting Statement A plus package; underlying cited sources not all independently retrieved. Specific corroboration recorded separately.

score_rationale.reproducibility: Small model exposes plans, participants, preparation and mailing time; display rounds total hours.
score_rationale.provenance: Investigation counts 2019–2024, postage and agency labor methodology cited; electronic shares inherited.
score_rationale.segmentation: Preparation and paper distribution separated proportionately.
score_rationale.labor: Accountant/clerk costs linked to EBSA common methodology; current rate derivation not reproduced locally.
score_rationale.item13: Mail volume, page price and postage are explicit; zero capital follows existing settlement process.
score_rationale.item14: Explains no additional government cost within an existing settlement process.
score_rationale.item15: Old/new totals and drivers supplied; no isolated decomposition for electronic delivery versus population.
score_rationale.validation: 13 observed investigations over six years support conservative rounding from 2.2 to 3 plans.
score_rationale.consistency: Formula label omits postage factor but numerical cost includes it; rounded hours explain apparent discrepancy.

item14.rationale: Existing investigation and settlement process; no additional federal collection cost

item15.reason: Population, wages, postage and electronic-delivery share updates

assumptions: Electronic delivery 96.1% combines 58.3% and 37.8% under separate safe-harbor assumptions.
13 investigations over six years rounded upward to 3 annually.

reconstruction_issues: Item 13 table formula label omits the postage term although the calculated value includes it.
Electronic-delivery shares require mutually exclusive population definitions before being added.
methods_worth_testing: A small collection can be highly reconstructable with a compact, empirically supported model.
Document conservative rounding separately from measured administrative counts.
